chapters.title: Chapter 2: The Main Types of Real Estate

lessons.title: Residential Property: Apartments, Villas and Plotted Developments

children.text: Three friends in Bengaluru each have about ₹1.2 crore to put into property. Ananya buys a 3BHK apartment in a high-rise near Hebbal. Vikram buys a gated-community villa off Sarjapur Road. Sneha buys a plot in an approved layout near Devanahalli. Same city, same budget, three completely different investments. Each one differs in what they actually own, how much rent they can earn, what it costs to hold, and how easily they can sell. This lesson breaks down all three.

body.text: Every residential property is two assets bundled together: land, which can appreciate, and a building, which wears out. The format you choose decides how much of your money goes into each.

children.text: The Three Formats at a Glance

cells: What you own
A flat plus an undivided share of the land
A house plus the land it stands on
Land only
Rental income
Highest and easiest to find tenants

None until you build

Society maintenance, property tax
Higher upkeep, community charges if gated
Low: property tax, fencing, occasional clearing
Liquidity
Best of the three in cities
Slower; fewer buyers at villa prices
Varies widely; can be very slow
Home loan
Widely available
Widely available
Plot loans are harder, often with lower loan-to-value
Main risk
Building ageing, society disputes, oversupply
High ticket, maintenance, narrow resale market

body.title: Rough share of your money going into land (illustrative, %)

children.text: These percentages are illustrative and vary enormously by city and location, but the direction holds. The more people share a piece of land, the smaller your slice of it, and the more of your money is tied up in concrete that ages every year.
Apartments: Know What You Are Paying For

markDefs.definition: The net usable floor area of a flat, excluding external walls, service shafts, exclusive balconies and open terraces, but including internal partition walls. The area RERA requires developers to sell on.
Carpet area plus the thickness of the flat's walls and, depending on the developer, balconies.
Built-up area plus a proportionate share of common areas like lobbies, staircases, lifts, the clubhouse and sometimes the swimming pool.

children.text: Flat sizes in India are quoted in three different ways, and the gap between them is where many buyers overpay.
Carpet area
is what you actually live in.
Built-up area
adds walls.
Super built-up area
adds your share of the lobby, lifts and clubhouse. Brokers love quoting super built-up area because it makes the flat sound bigger and the price per square foot sound smaller.

body.label: What RERA changed
body.value: Developers must sell on carpet area
body.context: Under the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016, the agreement for sale must state the carpet area. Resale deals and older projects may still be quoted on super built-up area, so always ask for the carpet area in writing.

body.caption: Loading of 25% to 40% is common in Indian apartment projects; higher loading means you pay for more space you do not live in.

children.text: Worked example: a resale flat in Kharadi, Pune is advertised at 1,400 sq ft for ₹1.4 crore, or "just ₹10,000 per sq ft." The carpet area turns out to be 1,000 sq ft. Loading is (1,400 minus 1,000) ÷ 1,000 = 40%. The real price per usable square foot is ₹1.4 crore ÷ 1,000 = ₹14,000, not ₹10,000.

body.title: Find the real rate
body.prompt: A flat in Thane is quoted at ₹9,500 per sq ft on a super built-up area of 1,250 sq ft. Its carpet area is 950 sq ft. What is the effective price per sq ft of carpet area, in ₹?
body.explanation: Total price = 1,250 × ₹9,500 = ₹1,18,75,000. Effective carpet rate = ₹1,18,75,000 ÷ 950 = ₹12,500 per sq ft. That is about 32% more than the quoted rate. Always compare flats on carpet area price, never on super built-up price.

children.text: The Land Hidden Inside Your Flat

markDefs.definition: Undivided Share of Land: the proportion of a project's total land that legally belongs to each flat owner. It cannot be separated or sold on its own.
Floor Space Index (also called Floor Area Ratio): the total built-up area permitted on a plot divided by the plot's area. Higher FSI means taller or denser buildings.

children.text: When you buy a flat, you also buy a slice of the land underneath the entire project, called your
UDS
. It is usually allocated in proportion to your flat's size. The higher the
FSI
a developer uses, the more flats share the same land, and the smaller each owner's UDS becomes.

body.latex: \text{UDS} = \frac{\text{Your Flat's Area}}{\text{Total Saleable Area of Project}} \times \text{Total Land Area}
body.caption: Check the UDS figure in your sale deed. In some states, such as Tamil Nadu, it is registered separately.

body.title: Calculate your UDS
body.prompt: A Chennai project sits on 80,000 sq ft of land with a total saleable area of 4,00,000 sq ft. Your flat is 1,600 sq ft. What is your undivided share of land, in sq ft?
body.explanation: 1,600 ÷ 4,00,000 × 80,000 = 320 sq ft. Your ₹1 crore-plus flat carries about 320 sq ft of land. That small slice is the part of your investment that does not age.

body.text: UDS explains why 40-year-old flats in Bandra or Dadar can still sell at high prices. The building is tired, but the land under it in a prime location is extremely valuable. In Mumbai, many old housing societies go for redevelopment: a developer demolishes the building, gives existing members larger new flats, and sells the extra flats that higher FSI allows. The land did the heavy lifting, not the concrete.

children.text: Villas and Independent Houses

A villa gives you your own land, your own walls and no neighbours above or below. In a gated villa community, such as those along Sarjapur Road in Bengaluru or Kokapet in Hyderabad, you also get shared security, roads and a clubhouse. Because a larger share of the price is land, villas tend to hold value well in growing areas. But they come with trade-offs investors often underestimate.

columns.label: Strengths
points: Bigger land share, which supports long-term appreciation
No dependence on a large society for decisions
Freedom to extend or rebuild within local rules
Scarce supply in well-located city pockets

columns.label: Weaknesses
points: Higher ticket size, so more concentration risk
Rental yields often lower than apartments at the same price
Repairs, painting and waterproofing are all on you
Fewer buyers can afford it, so resale can take longer

body.title: Villa vs apartment yield
body.prompt: A ₹1.2 crore villa off Sarjapur Road rents for ₹30,000 a month. A ₹1.2 crore 3BHK apartment in Hebbal rents for ₹38,000 a month. By how many percentage points is the apartment's gross yield higher? Round to one decimal place.
body.explanation: Villa: ₹3,60,000 ÷ ₹1,20,00,000 = 3.0%. Apartment: ₹4,56,000 ÷ ₹1,20,00,000 = 3.8%. The apartment earns 0.8 percentage points more in rent. The villa owner is betting more heavily on land appreciation to make up the gap.

children.text: Plotted Developments: Pure Land, Pure Risk

markDefs.definition: A large piece of land divided by a developer into individual residential plots, with internal roads, drainage, water and electricity lines, sanctioned by the local planning authority.

children.text: A
plotted development

sells you land with basic infrastructure, and you build whenever you choose. Plots have no building to depreciate, no society to manage and very low holding costs, which is why they have long been popular with Indian investors in Hyderabad, Chennai, Bengaluru, Lucknow and Jaipur. Developers have taken note: ANAROCK reports that a significant portion of recent land buying by developers is being directed towards plotted and villa formats.

stats.context: 32 deals, the highest among the top seven cities

body.text: Plots are where the most expensive mistakes in Indian real estate happen. The same land can be sold to two buyers, plots can sit in layouts with no planning approval, and agricultural land is sometimes sold as "residential plots" without legal conversion. An empty plot can also be encroached on while you are not watching. A plot is only as good as its title and approvals, which you will learn to check in Chapter 4.

body.caption: Approvals a genuine residential plot should have

cells: Layout approval
Sanction from the local planning body, such as DTCP, HMDA, BMRDA, BDA, CMDA or a development authority
Unapproved layouts can be denied building permission, utilities and bank loans
Land use
Land classified or converted for residential use
Agricultural land cannot legally be used for housing without conversion
RERA registration
Project number on the state RERA website, where the project is large enough to require it
RERA gives you legal remedies against the developer
Clear title
Unbroken ownership chain and an encumbrance certificate
Protects against double sale and existing loans on the land
Infrastructure
Roads, drainage, water and power actually built, not just promised
Plots without infrastructure are hard to build on or sell

body.title: Other residential formats you will hear about

children.text: Studio and 1BHK apartments:
Small, lower-ticket units near job hubs. They often rent easily and at higher yields, but appreciate slowly and attract a narrower pool of buyers.
Co-living:
Buildings leased to operators who rent beds or rooms to young professionals. Income depends heavily on the operator's health.
Serviced and holiday homes:
Units in Goa, Lonavala or the hills rented out by the night. Returns swing with tourist seasons, and management fees can be steep.
Senior living:
Communities designed for retirees, with healthcare and services. A growing niche, but resale is limited to a specific buyer group.
Managed farmland:
Agricultural land sold in small pieces with farming services. Many states restrict who can buy agricultural land, so the legal structure needs very careful checking.

body.title: Which area is it?
body.question: A broker says a flat is 1,500 sq ft, including its share of the lobby, lifts and clubhouse. Which measurement is the broker quoting?
body.explanation: Super built-up area includes a share of common areas like lobbies, lifts and the clubhouse. Always ask for the carpet area, which RERA requires in the agreement for sale.

body.title: The ageing component
body.textWithBlank: In any residential property, the land can appreciate over time, while the ___ wears out and loses value as it ages.
body.explanation: Buildings depreciate physically and become dated. Land does not. That is why formats with a larger land share, like villas and plots, rely more on appreciation, while apartments trade land share for rental income and convenience.

body.title: The three Bengaluru friends, ten years on
body.scenario: Recall Ananya (3BHK apartment near Hebbal), Vikram (villa off Sarjapur Road) and Sneha (approved plot near Devanahalli), each with about ₹1.2 crore. Ten years later, all three need to sell within three months to fund a child's overseas education.
body.prompt: Based on this lesson, how is each friend likely placed, and what would have helped each of them?
body.modelAnswer:
1. Ananya (apartment): best placed to sell quickly, since city apartments have the largest buyer pool and home loans are easy for buyers. She also earned the most rent over ten years. Her risk is that the 10-year-old building now competes with newer projects, and her small UDS limits land-driven gains.
2. Vikram (villa): may have seen solid land-driven appreciation, but at a high ticket size the buyer pool is narrow, so a three-month deadline could force a discount. He earned less rent and spent more on upkeep.
3. Sneha (plot): has had almost no holding costs and no rent. Her outcome depends heavily on whether the area around Devanahalli developed as expected. Plot resale can be slow, and buyers will scrutinise title and approvals, so clean documents are essential.
4. What would have helped all three: matching the format to their likely need for cash, keeping an emergency fund so they were never forced sellers, and choosing locations with proven demand rather than promised infrastructure.

body.title: Before You Pick a Residential Format
steps: Decide whether you want rental income, appreciation, or a future home
Get the carpet area in writing and calculate the price per carpet sq ft
For apartments, find your UDS and the society's monthly maintenance
For villas, estimate yearly upkeep and check local rents for similar homes
For plots, confirm layout approval, land use, RERA registration and clear title
Ask how quickly similar properties in the area have actually resold

body.label: MahaRERA: Search Registered Projects
body.description: Look up a Maharashtra project's RERA registration, carpet areas and approvals. Other states run similar RERA portals.

cards.definition: The usable floor area inside a flat's walls. RERA requires developers to sell on carpet area.
Carpet area plus walls plus a share of common areas like lobbies, lifts and the clubhouse.
The extra percentage of super built-up area over carpet area. Higher loading means paying for more non-usable space.
Undivided Share of Land: each flat owner's proportional ownership of the project's land.
Floor Space Index: permitted built-up area divided by plot area. It controls how densely land can be built on.
Land divided into approved residential plots with roads and utilities, where buyers build their own homes.
Demolishing an old building and rebuilding it with more FSI, common in Mumbai, where existing owners get new, often larger flats.

points: Every residential property bundles appreciating land with a depreciating building.
Apartments offer the best rent and liquidity, but a small land share; villas and plots put more of your money into land.
Compare flats on price per carpet sq ft. Loading of 25% to 40% can make a flat far more expensive than it looks.
Your UDS is the land you really own in an apartment project, and it drives long-term and redevelopment value.
Villas typically earn lower yields and have a narrower resale market, balanced by a larger land share.
Plots have no rent and low holding costs, but carry the highest legal risk: verify approvals, land use and title.

body.text: This lesson is for education only and is not investment or legal advice. Prices, rents, land shares and approval rules vary by state, city and project. Verify documents with a qualified property lawyer and consult a SEBI-registered investment adviser before making investment decisions.
